native_retrieval.title: China's coronavirus lockdown strategy: brutal but effective | Coronavirus | The Guardian
native_retrieval.snippet: The world was astonished by the Wuhan quarantine but it seems to have worked. When China announced it was shutting down Wuhan, the centre of the coronavirus outbreak, in a bid to prevent further spread of the disease, the world was stunned and experts sceptical. Wuhan alone has a population of 11 million, and tens of millions more people in nearby cities were soon brought under lockdown as well, as the scale of the crisis became apparent. Countries with their own exponentially-growing outbreaks are imposing similar measures, from Italy and Spain to Germany and California, though none are as strict as Wuhan’s. Starting within hours of the announcement, transport into and out of the city was closed, with no exceptions even for personal and medical emergencies. Controls were stepped up elsewhere across China soon after Wuhan was locked down, in part because of fears that people racing to escape the city before it was closed off could have turbo-charged the spread of Covid-19.
